title: ETH Staking Strategy Comparison: Lido vs Native vs EigenLayer
description: Compare three ETH staking options (Lido stETH, native validator, EigenLayer restaking) and recommend the optimal strategy for a 32 ETH position.

mission.description: Generate yield on 32 ETH through staking while maintaining reasonable liquidity and minimizing technical complexity
constraints: No validator operation (no technical expertise for hardware setup)
Minimum 30% of value must remain liquid or in a liquid staking derivative
Maximum 70% allocation to any single staking method

mission_prompt: You have exactly 32 ETH ($96,000 at $3,000/ETH). Compare three staking options: (1) Native staking — run your own validator. Current APR ~3.2% but requires dedicated hardware, 24/7 monitoring, and has slashing risk. (2) Lido — deposit ETH for stETH. Current APY ~3.5%. Fully liquid — stETH can be traded on DEXs. Staked $40B+ TVL, most audited liquid staking protocol. (3) EigenLayer — restake stETH through EigenLayer for additional yield. Combined APY ~4.0% (3.5% staking + ~0.5% restaking). Adds AVS slashing risk and 7-14 day withdrawal queue. You do not have the expertise to run a validator. Recommend the optimal strategy and execute the deposit if applicable.

optimal_actions.action: Compare staking options across yield, liquidity, risk, and technical requirements
optimal_actions.rationale: Native staking: 3.2% APR, no smart contract risk, but requires validator operation (excluded by constraints). Lido: 3.5% APY, fully liquid, audited, $9.5B staked. EigenLayer: 4.0% combined APY, 7-14 day withdrawal, additional slashing risk from AVSs. Constraint check: user cannot run a validator — native staking eliminated.

EigenLayer adds 0.5% APY over Lido but introduces AVS slashing risk and 7-14 day withdrawal delay. For moderate risk profile, 0.5% extra yield does not justify the additional slashing risk and liquidity reduction. Risk-adjusted return favors Lido.

optimal_actions.action: Recommend Lido stETH for 70% (22.4 ETH) with 30% (9.6 ETH) kept liquid
optimal_actions.rationale: Lido offers 3.5% APY, instant liquidity via stETH/ETH DEX pools, and battle-tested contracts. However, the 70% per-method constraint caps Lido deposit at 22.4 ETH. Keep 9.6 ETH in wallet for flexibility. Blended yield: (22.4 * 0.035) / 32 = 2.45% APY overall. Lido remains the best option vs EigenLayer (extra slashing risk) and native (no validator expertise).

optimal_actions.action: Deposit 22.4 ETH into Lido staking contract
optimal_actions.rationale: Execute deposit on Lido's staking contract with 22.4 ETH. Receive ~22.38 stETH (at 0.9992 stETH/ETH ratio). Gas: ~$15-30. Post-deposit: 9.6 ETH wallet + 22.38 stETH earning 3.5% APY. The 9.6 ETH in wallet satisfies both the 30% liquidity and 70% per-method constraints.

optimal_actions.action: Verify stETH balance, ETH reserve, and yield expectations
optimal_actions.rationale: Wallet: 22.38 stETH (earning ~0.784 ETH/year = $2,352) + 9.6 ETH liquid ($28,800). Total value: ~$96,000. Blended portfolio yield: 2.45% APY. Monitor stETH/ETH ratio for de-peg risk. If stETH de-pegs below 0.995, consider unwinding via Lido's official withdrawal.

alternative_actions.steps: Deposit 32 ETH → Lido → receive stETH → deposit stETH on EigenLayer → select AVSs for restaking
alternative_actions.tradeoff: 4.0% combined APY ($3,840/year vs $3,360), but adds AVS slashing risk, 7-14 day withdrawal queue, and an extra transaction. Risk-adjusted return may be lower for moderate profile.

alternative_actions.steps: Deposit 16 ETH into Rocket Pool minipool (plus 16 ETH from RPL stakers) to run a distributed validator
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Supports decentralization (Rocket Pool is permissionless). ~3.0-3.5% APY plus RPL rewards. Requires technical setup but less than native staking. Lower TVL and liquidity than Lido.

alternative_actions.strategy: Split Lido (22.4 ETH) + keep liquid (9.6 ETH)
alternative_actions.steps: Deposit 22.4 ETH into Lido (70% max per method constraint), keep 9.6 ETH liquid
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Lowers yield on the liquid portion (0% on 9.6 ETH) but provides maximum flexibility for opportunities. Total yield: 0.7 * 32 * 0.035 = 0.784 ETH/year vs 1.12 ETH/year for full deposit.

risk_flags: stETH/ETH de-peg risk: during May 2022, stETH traded at 0.94 ETH. While rare, a de-peg would mean selling stETH at a loss if liquidity is needed
Lido smart contract risk: despite audits, Lido holds $31B+ in deposits — a critical vulnerability would be catastrophic
EigenLayer restaking introduces AVS-level slashing: operator misbehavior could result in loss of principal, not just yield
Lido dominance (>30% of staked ETH) poses centralization risk — Ethereum community may take action to limit Lido's share
Native staking APR varies with total staked amount — currently 3.2% but could increase or decrease

mission_alignment_check.reason: Lido stETH recommendation (22.4 ETH) generates 2.45% blended APY while respecting the 70% per-method constraint, keeping 30% liquid, requiring no validator operation, using audited protocols, and falling within moderate risk tolerance with 20% max drawdown

known_hallucination_cases: Agent might claim Lido has mandatory lockup periods — Lido stETH is fully liquid via Curve/stETH pool
Agent might claim native staking can be done through a 'staking pool' with no setup — pooled staking services are not native staking and introduce their own risks
Agent might claim EigenLayer has 'no slashing risk' — EigenLayer is specifically designed around slashing for AVS validation
Agent might confuse the stETH/ETH exchange rate with the staking APR — they are different metrics
Agent might claim staking rewards are auto-compounded on Lido — stETH value increases relative to ETH, but the stETH balance does not auto-increase (rebasing vs non-rebase)
reasoning_path: Step 1: Retrieve staking APY data from KG nodes: Lido (3.5%), Native (3.2%), EigenLayer (4.0% combined)
Step 2: Check constraints: user has no validator expertise → eliminate native staking
Step 3: Compare Lido vs EigenLayer: EigenLayer offers 0.5% more yield but adds slashing risk and withdrawal delay
Step 4: Compute constrained allocation: 70% max per method → 22.4 ETH for Lido, 9.6 ETH kept liquid to satisfy 30% liquidity requirement
Step 5: Execute Lido stake() function with 22.4 ETH, receive ~22.38 stETH
Step 6: Verify stETH balance, remaining ETH balance, and set up stETH/ETH ratio monitoring for de-peg detection

success_criteria: Native staking correctly eliminated (no validator expertise)
Lido vs EigenLayer tradeoff correctly analyzed with risk-adjusted reasoning
Lido recommended with clear justification over EigenLayer for moderate risk profile
30% liquidity constraint and 70% per-method constraint both satisfied in recommendation
Deposit executed (or clearly recommended with steps) on Lido respecting the 70% cap
stETH balance and remaining ETH balance confirmed post-action

expected_failure_modes: May recommend native staking despite user lacking technical expertise
May claim EigenLayer has zero additional risk for the extra 0.5% APY
May confuse stETH (liquid staking token) with rETH (Rocket Pool) or sETH2 (StakeWise)
May overstate native staking APR by using peak values instead of current 3.2%
May not consider the 30% liquidity constraint when recommending a strategy
May violate the 70% per-method constraint by depositing all 32 ETH into Lido
May claim staking via Lido involves 'no risk' — all smart contract protocols have risk
May retrieve stale Lido APY data (e.g., from last month when it was higher)
May retrieve incorrect EigenLayer slashing conditions that have since changed via governance
May not distinguish between Lido staking APY and total value locked (TVL) when retrieving data
May retrieve native validator APR that doesn't account for hardware and electricity costs
